newsitem.title: CHINA: Ericsson in $137 million China deals.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson in $137 million China deals.

text.p: Swedish telecommunications group Ericsson has signed contracts worth a combined $137 million with four Chinese provinces, the Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.

Ericsson signed the contracts this month to provide mobile telecommunications system expansion programmes to Inner Mongolia and Hebei in the north, Liaoning in the northeast and Qinghai in the west, Xinhua said.
The deals were scheduled to be completed either in 1997 or 1998, it said but gave no further details of the deals.
China is Ericsson's second largest market in the world after the United States. Its mobile communications systems cover 20 Chinese provinces.
Ericsson could not be reached for comment.
China's cellular telephone subscribers totalled 6.8 million by the end of 1996. The figure is forecast to exceed 20 million by the year 2000, Xinhua said.
China plans to increase the number of new subscribers by four million in 1997, Minister of Post and Telecommunications Wu Jichuan has said.
